title: Canonical QCoh comparison lifts
statement:
In the canonical qcqs rectangle setting, using the QCoh restrictions [lem-sc-duality-base-change-inverse-square-mate], pinned pullback composition [lem-pc-ringed-spaces-derived-pullback-composition], and pinned adjunctions [def-pc-derived-base-change-map], there exist comparison isomorphisms p:L⋙Q≅P and b:B≅H whose inclusion maps have the unit/conjugate and inverse composition component formulas displayed below. This construction assumes no invertibility of base-change maps. The complete quantified formula is:
theorem rectangle_qcoh_comparison_lifts
    [∀ Z : Scheme.{u}, HasDerivedCategory.{w} (SheafOfModules.{u} (moduleRings Z.toRingedSpace))]
    {X Y S T : Scheme.{u}}
    [CompactSpace X] [QuasiSeparatedSpace X] [CompactSpace Y] [QuasiSeparatedSpace Y]
    [CompactSpace S] [QuasiSeparatedSpace S] [CompactSpace T] [QuasiSeparatedSpace T]
    (f : X ⟶ Y) [QuasiCompact f] [QuasiSeparated f]
    (g : S ⟶ Y) (h : T ⟶ S)
    (k : pullback (pullback.snd f g) h ⟶ pullback f (h ≫ g))
    (hk₁ : k ≫ pullback.fst f (h ≫ g) =
      pullback.fst (pullback.snd f g) h ≫ pullback.fst f g)
    (hk₂ : k ≫ pullback.snd f (h ≫ g) = pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h) :
    let U := qcPullback (pullback.fst f (h ≫ g))
    let L := qcPullback k
    let V := qcPullback (pullback.fst f g) ⋙
      qcPullback (pullback.fst (pullback.snd f g) h)
    let P := @qcDirectImage _ _ _ _
      (quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g))) _ _
      (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g))
    let Q := @qcDirectImage _ _ _ _
      (quasiSeparatedSpace_of_quasiSeparated (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h)) _ _
      (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h)
    let B := qcPullback (h ≫ g)
    let H := qcPullback g ⋙ qcPullback h
    let c := @Classical.choose _ _ (Classical.choose_spec (Classical.choose_spec
      (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition.{u, w})))
    let a := fun {A B : Scheme.{u}} (r : A ⟶ B) ↦
      Classical.choose (exists_schemeDerivedAdjunction r
        (hAdd := (Classical.choose exists_derivedPullbackComposition) r)
        ((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition)) r)
        ((Classical.choose (Classical.choose_spec
          (Classical.choose_spec exists_derivedPullbackComposition))) r))
    let d := conjugateIsoEquiv (a (pullback.snd (pullback.snd f g) h))
      ((a (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g))).comp (a k))
      (c k (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g)) ≪≫
        eqToIso (congrArg (fun r ↦ derivedPullback.{u, w} r) hk₂))
    ∃ (p : L ⋙ Q ≅ P) (b : B ≅ H),
      (∀ D : schemeDerivedQCohCategory (pullback f (h ≫ g)),
        (schemeDerivedQCohProperty T).ι.map (p.inv.app D) =
          (schemeDerivedDirectImage (pullback.snd f (h ≫ g))).map
            ((a k).unit.app D.obj) ≫ d.inv.app ((derivedPullback k).obj D.obj)) ∧
      (∀ D : schemeDerivedQCohCategory Y,
        (schemeDerivedQCohProperty T).ι.map (b.hom.app D) = (c h g).inv.app D.obj)

proof.text: The two projection equations identify k with pullbackLeftPullbackSndIso.hom, by the uniqueness clause for the outer pullback. Pullback along k is an equivalence: its inverse is pullback along the inverse scheme isomorphism, with unit and counit obtained from the pinned composition and identity comparisons. Consequently the unit of the pinned adjunction for k is invertible. Conjugate c(k,q) followed by the transport along hk₂ under the pinned adjunctions for q, k, and the iterated second projection; this is d. Whisker d with pullback along k and cancel the invertible unit to obtain an ambient isomorphism from that pullback followed by the iterated direct image to the outer direct image. Its inverse component is exactly the first displayed formula. Both end functors preserve quasi-coherent objects, so full faithfulness of the QCoh inclusion lifts this isomorphism uniquely to p. Likewise lift c(h,g).symm to b. Faithfulness gives the second component formula. No base-change map is assumed invertible here. Empty schemes and identity maps satisfy the same universal-property and adjunction calculations.
